endorsements.quote: Patients may benefit from understanding that LLMs are optimized for user satisfaction, are prone to agreeing with the user’s framing [ 32 ], and can generate convincing inaccuracies.

unlisted_practices: Make structured inquiry into patients' AI use a routine element of OCRD intake and case conceptualization.
Do not certify or recommend specific AI products to patients; frame recommendations around the function a patient seeks rather than a named product.
Extend response prevention to AI use through a graded hierarchy, prioritizing graded response prevention and behavioral experiments over system configuration.
Target only maladaptive AI use functions in treatment and preserve adaptive uses of AI.
Ask patients directly about their safety-relevant exchanges with LLMs and how the LLM responded.
Assess the patient-AI relationship at baseline in OCRD studies and specify the estimand before selecting an adjustment strategy.
Record primary AI product and version, model updates or retirement during assessment, product switching, and baseline domain profile as covariates in studies involving AI use.
Advise patients to assume information given to commercial LLMs is stored and outside clinical confidentiality, and discuss data privacy with them.
Sample across diverse clinical settings when validating and deploying AI-relationship assessment frameworks.

screen.reason: Perspective/framework paper proposing a cognitive-behavioral framework to conceptualize, assess, and safeguard against patient-AI dynamics (reassurance seeking) in OCRD.
